facts.text: Appellant Harbhajan Singh was convicted for an offence under Section 500 of the Indian Penal Code.

J.,By this appeal, which has been brought to this Court by special leave, the appellant Harbhajan Singh challenges the companyrectness of his companyviction for an offence under S. 500 07 the Indian Penal Code, and the sentence imposed on him for the said offence.

facts.text: Criminal proceedings started on a complaint filed by Surinder Singh Kairon, son of S. Partap Singh Kairon, Chief Minister of Punjab.

anchor.surface_text: The criminal proceedings against the appellant were started on a companyplaint filed by Surinder Singh Kairon, son of S. Partap Singh Kairon, who was at the relevant time the Chief Minister of the State of Punjab. In his companyplaint, the companyplainant Surinder Singh alleged that the appellant had published in the Press a statement against him which was highly defamatory of him.

facts.text: Appellant published a defamatory statement against Surinder Singh Kairon in Blitz weekly magazine on July 23, 1957.

anchor.surface_text: The said statement was published in the Blitz, which is a weekly magazine of Bombay, on July 23, 1957, and extracts from it were given publicity in the Times of India and certain other papers. According to the, companyplaint, the defamatory statement was, absolutely untrue and by publishing it, the appellant had rendered himself liable to be punished under s. 500, I.P.C.

facts.text: Punjab Government issued a Press Note on July 22/23, 1957, denying complicity of a Minister's son in smuggling and challenging newspapers to name him openly.

anchor.surface_text: It appears that on July 2,2/23, 1957, the punjab Government issued a Press numbere in which it was averred that certain Urdu Dailies from Jullundur were indulging in mischief and false propaganda, alleging companyplicity of a Ministers son in smuggling on the border. The Press numbere alleged that this was done with a view to malign the Government and to cause suspicion in the mind of public.

facts.text: Appellant's impugned statement named Surinder Singh Kairon as the son of the Minister involved in smuggling and responsible for crimes in Punjab.

anchor.surface_text: It was in response to the challenge thus issued by the Punjab Government in its Press numbere that the appellant published impugned statement which reads My attention has been drawn to a Punjab Government Press Note categorically denying the companyplicity of a Ministers son in smuggling. That Press Note also throws a challenge to some Urdu Dailies to companye out openly with the name of the son of the Minister and then base the companysequences.

facts.text: Mr. Ajaib Singh, Senior Superintendent of Police, Amritsar, issued a statement on July 25, 1957, denying Minister's son's involvement in smuggling.

anchor.surface_text: After this statement was published, Mr. Ajaib Singh, Senior Superintendent of Police, Amritsar, issued a statement on the 25th July, 1957, which was published in the Tribune on the 26th July. By this statement, Mr. Ajaib Singh assured the people that persons companycerned in smuggling cases had been interrogated and he was satisfied that the allegation that some Ministers son was involved in smuggling was false and inaccurate.

facts.text: Appellant issued a rejoinder published in Hind Samachar on July 27, 1957.

anchor.surface_text: To this statement, the appelLant issued a rejoinder which was published in the Hind Samachar, which is an Urdu Daily of Jullundur, on July 27, 1957. Then, followed the companyplaint which was filed by the companyplainant on August 17, 1957.

facts.text: Complaint filed by Surinder Singh on August 17, 1957, in court of Magistrate, First Class, Tarn Taran.

anchor.surface_text: Then, followed the companyplaint which was filed by the companyplainant on August 17, 1957. That, shortly stated, is the background of the present criminal proceedings. The companyplaint was filed in the companyrt of the Magistrate, First Class, Tar, Taran.

facts.text: Supreme Court directed on October 4, 1957, transfer of case to Punjab High Court for further transfer to Sessions Court in Delhi.

anchor.surface_text: Thereafter, the appellant moved this Court under s. 527 of the Criminal Procedure Code for the transfer of the said case from the companyrt of the Magistrate where it had been tiled. This Court directed on October 4, 1957, that the case in question should be remitted to the Punjab High Court so that it should be transferred by the said High Court from the companyrt of the Magistrate at Tarn Taran to a companyrt of Sessions in Delhi.

facts.text: Case tried by Additional Sessions Judge, Delhi, who convicted appellant and sentenced to one year simple imprisonment.

anchor.surface_text: That is how the case was transferred to the companyrt of the Additional Sessions Judge, Delhi, and was tried by him. ... In the result, he companyvicted the appellant and sentenced him to one years simple imprisonment.

facts.text: Punjab High Court confirmed conviction but reduced sentence to three months simple imprisonment and fine of Rs. 2,000 on November 25, 1960.

anchor.surface_text: In the result, the High Court companyfirmed the order of companyviction passed against the appellant by the trial Judge, but ordered that instead of undergoing one years simple imprisonment, the appellant shall undergo three months simple imprisonment and pay a fine of Rs. 2,000.

facts.text: Appellant claimed protection of Ninth Exception to Section 499 IPC, alleging good faith and public good.

anchor.surface_text: In substance, he alleged that the allegations made by him in his impugned statement were true and he had published the said allegations in the interest of public good. In other words, he claimed the protection of the First Exception to s. 499, IPC. He also pleaded that the imputation which he had made against the companyplainant had been made in good faith and for public good.
